newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add temporary reserves to the banking system Wednesday via overnight system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
"I'm looking for the Fed to inject reserves through an overnight system RP today," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
Analysts at consulting firm MMS International Inc expect the Fed to add reserves either through customer or system repurchase agreements.
At 1000 EST/1500 GMT, the federal funds rate was quoted at 5-5/16 percent, above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target.
With funds trading at high levels, analysts did not discount the possibility of a Fed move before the central bank's usual intervention time of 1130.
Analysts estimated the Fed's add need Wednesday at around $3.0 billion. Going forward, they said the central bank will still have to cope with large add needs.
"In the (two-week reserve maintenance) period beginning tomorrow we see a daily average add need of around $9.0 billion," Saporta said.
Analysts still expect the Fed to add permanent reserves to the system via a coupon pass operation Wednesday.
